Risk Summary: Public S3 bucket exposes customer reports
Remediation Recommendation: Remove the public-read bucket policy; re-enable Block Public Access at bucket and account level; enable S3 default encryption (SSE-KMS).

Risk Summary: AdministratorAccess role on internet-facing web host
Remediation Recommendation: Replace AdministratorAccess on meridian-ec2-app-role with a policy scoped to the exact S3 read and CloudWatch Logs write the app needs; attach a permissions boundary; add a detective alert on iam:AttachRolePolicy / iam:PutRolePolicy for this role.
Remove the 0.0.0.0/0 rule on web-sg TCP 22. Prefer AWS Systems Manager Session Manager for shell access (no inbound port). If SSH must stay, restrict source to a bastion or VPN CIDR /32.
Set IMDSv2 to Required on the instance (done). Also set the account-level IMDS default to require IMDSv2 for new instances and reduce the metadata hop limit to 1.

Register an MFA device for Callum-v2 now and attach a policy denying actions when aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent is false. Longer term, move console access to IAM Identity Center / federation and retire the static user.

Risk Summary: Privilege-escalation path via Callum-v2 inline policies
Remediation Recommendation: Remove the AltPermsEC2 and EC2Perm inline policies from Callum-v2 (or reduce to ec2:Describe* read-only). Attach a permissions boundary. Alert on ec2:ModifyInstanceAttribute, ec2:AssociateIamInstanceProfile and iam:PutUserPolicy.
Register a virtual MFA device for meridian-analyst-1. Enforce MFA for all console users via an account-wide deny-without-MFA IAM policy (covers R-16 too).
Enable VPC flow logs on meridian-vpc to CloudWatch Logs (or S3) with 90-day retention. Alert on rejected traffic toward the private (DB) subnet.

Risk Summary: No monitoring or alerting on account activity
Remediation Recommendation: Deliver CloudTrail to CloudWatch Logs. Create CIS-aligned metric filters and alarms: root usage, unauthorised API calls, IAM policy changes, security-group and NACL changes, console sign-in without MFA, CMK disable / scheduled deletion. Consider enabling GuardDuty.

Retire the long-lived access keys. Move the local CLI to short-lived credentials via IAM Identity Center (aws sso) or role assumption. If a static key must remain, cap age at 90 days and alert on key age via the IAM credential report.

Risk Summary: S3 bucket hardening gaps (transport, versioning, logging)
Remediation Recommendation: Add an aws:SecureTransport=false Deny statement to both bucket policies. Enable object versioning (and MFA Delete) on the CloudTrail log bucket. Enable S3 server access logging on both buckets.
Enable account-level EBS default encryption. Re-create the two instance root volumes from encrypted snapshots (stop instance, snapshot, copy with encryption, create volume, detach/attach).
Set the IAM account password policy: minimum length 14, require upper / lower / number / symbol, prevent reuse of last 24, maximum age 90 days.

Risk Summary: Root account: virtual (not hardware) MFA and routine use
Remediation Recommendation: Register a FIDO2 / hardware security key as the root MFA device. Stop using root for routine operations - operate via a dedicated admin identity or federated admin role. Alert on any root console sign-in.

Review DemoEC2 and aws-ec2-spot-fleet-tagging-role: confirm owner and purpose, delete if unused. For any kept service role, add aws:SourceArn / aws:SourceAccount conditions. Institute a quarterly IAM access review.
Enable automatic annual key rotation on the meridian CMK (single setting).
